opportunities.name: Tech project lead research (HN + GitHub → note)
opportunities.description: For a given open-source project name, find its top Hacker News story (points, age), open its GitHub repo to get the star count and latest release date, and save a 'Lead:' note.
steps: Open HN search (hn.algolia.com) and search for {project}
Note the top story's title, points and age
On GitHub, open 'Search or jump to', type {project} and press Enter
Read the star count and latest release date
In the notes app, add a new note: 'Lead: {project}. HN "{story title}" ({points} pts, {age}); GitHub {stars} stars, last release {date}'

instances.values: project=deno (only the GitHub search; no HN lookup or note, looks abandoned)

opportunities.name: Country fact-check (World Bank indicator + BBC context → note)
opportunities.description: For a given country, look up its life expectancy on World Bank Data, find a recent BBC story on '{country} {topic}', and save a 'Fact-check' note combining the two.
steps: On data.worldbank.org, type {country} in 'Search data' and press Enter, using the World Bank spelling (e.g. 'Viet Nam')
Open the country page and read life expectancy at birth with its year
On BBC, open the menu, search '{country} {topic}' and open the top relevant article
In the notes app, add a new note: 'Fact-check {country}: Life expectancy at birth {value} ({year}). Context: {headline} ({age})'

instances.values: country=Argentina (World Bank search only, retried several times; no BBC step or note)

opportunities.name: Company court-case pitch (CourtListener + Wikipedia → email)
opportunities.description: For a given company, search CourtListener for a case it was involved in, get company facts (HQ, CEO) from Wikipedia, and draft a pitch email to an editor.
steps: On CourtListener, type {company} in the keyword search and press Enter
Open a relevant case and note its name, court and filing date
On Wikipedia, search {company} and open the company article
In mail, compose to {editor email} with subject 'Pitch: {company} in court'
Body: 'Hi {name}, {case} ({court}, filed {date}). {company}: HQ {hq}, CEO {ceo}. Worth a piece?'

instances.values: company=Uber, case=Uber v. Uber (Ohio Ct. App. 2017), to=lena@example.com (draft was discarded)
company=Airbnb (CourtListener search only, re-run several times)
company=Tesla (CourtListener search, then Wikipedia 'Tesla, Inc.'; no email sent)
